changed.was: by its account the smoke comes from the malt, not from the coal; The coal fires heat the stills; they do not smoke the whisky. The peat comes from the malt, by Nikka's own account.
changed.now: its tasting note puts the smoky aroma down to the peat fires that dried the barley; Do not put Yoichi's smoke down to the coal alone: by Nikka's account the peat fires that dried the barley give the smoky aroma, and the coal fire adds depth and a subtle smokiness.
changed.why: Nikka's own pages credit the coal-fired distillation with depth and a subtle smokiness, so the record misstated the house's account

open: yamazaki: pure malt on the label until 2004 rests on VinePair and trade histories; 1923 is the start of building, trade sources give 1924 for the opening.
hakushu: Suntory names no cask for the 12; the pause of 2018 and the return of 2021 rest on news reports.
yoichi: the Important Cultural Property year is November 2021 (recommendation) or February 2022 (designation) by source, so none is given; Nikka names no casks.
miyagikyo: brought from Scotland in 1963 rests on Nikka's history alone; the 10 Years Old's return is 2025 in the United Kingdom and July 2026 in the United States, so no year is given.

mars: Mars Whisky as a label term was not seen on a photograph of the core label; 798 metres stands on a Hombo page under the Shinshu name; 1960 for Yamanashi rests on Master of Malt and the producer's history.
living: Met in sources and named in no record: none new; no living blender or distiller of Suntory, Nikka or Hombo appears in any record.

The dead met and named with dates: Shinjiro Torii (1879 to 1962), Keizo Saji (1919 to 1999), Masataka Taketsuru (1894 to 1979), Rita Cowan (1896 to 1961). The dead met and not named: Kiichiro Iwai of Settsu Shuzo and Mars (no death year in two sources), and Taketsuru's adopted son, whose recollection Nikka gives for the river water tale.
swaps: No swap proposed by the author and none made. The Yoichi and Miyagikyo no-age-statement bottlings stay: Nikka's expressions page lists both at 45%. Mars Single Malt Komagatake stays: the producer made it the core bottling of the brand in July 2025.
